Agreed next steps: benchmark prompt set, share security pack, internal pilot on dedicated 2x A100s or hosted burst, follow-up in 1 week.

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2028-01-05
Start: 14:30 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Alvarez (Redwood SE), Priya Patel (Redwood SE), Samir Kaur (Aurion Head of Product), Lena Ortiz (Aurion ML Eng), Tom Reeves (Aurion SRE), Aisha Mohammed (Aurion Security)

Auto-summary (auto-gen): Customer looking to choose models and deployment mode. Needs long context, multilingual, RAG/tool-calling. Interested in latency tradeoffs and private VPC due to EU data residency.

00:00 Samir: "Alright thanks everyone for jumping on, we wanted to make sure we had the right folks here to talk model choices and infra. We're spinning up a doc assistant and a search assistant, and for the doc assistant we have a lot of long contracts and regulatory files so context length is a big thing for us."

01:02 Maya: "Great, thanks Samir. Quick intros - I'm Maya, AE; Diego and Priya are our SEs who will do the deep bench and POC. Can you give us a little context on current stack?"

01:18 Lena: "Sure — we currently run a mixed stack. In prod we have a microservice that calls a third-party API, but for sensitivity reasons some docs can't leave our EU accounts. For development we've been prototyping with open weights — Llama-ish forks and a couple Mistral checkpoints — some fine tuned. Latency today is kind of all over the place, 500ms to 2s per call with cached short context. For the long docs we basically chunk which is messy. We want a model that can do native long context 32k or ideally 64k so we don't have to stitch too much."

02:45 Diego: "Do you have a target p95 latency for the doc assistant?"

02:52 Lena: "For user-facing UI we'd like p95 < 800ms for short queries and under 3s for long doc summarization. Cost matters; we don't want to blow up cloud bills. Also we need good Spanish and Chinese — at least parity with English."

03:30 Priya: "That helps. On the model front we usually recommend benchmarking a lightweight 13B open model and a larger 70B variant for quality comparison; some customers use 7B for extremely latency-sensitive flows. Important to know — tool calling, are you building out webhook-style actions or integrated DB retrieval?"

04:06 Samir: "Both. We need RAG with vector DB lookups and also tool calling to trigger internal workflows — e.g., create ticket, call internal API. Security is, of course, a blocker; we need audit trails and KMS integration."

04:34 Aisha: "Yes, on security: SOC 2 is table stakes, we also need enterprise SSO (SAML/SCIM), audit logs, and key management — can Redwood support customer-managed keys?"

04:50 Maya: "Short answer: yes. For Private we support customer KMS/HSM integrations; Dedicated also supports BYOK in many cases; Hosted supports encryption at rest and we offer a KMS integration path for enterprise. We'll send the exact matrix in the security pack."

05:20 Tom: "On networking — we prefer VPC peering over public egress for the pilot. We might require an on-prem box later for air-gapped workflows. How does Redwood handle private deployments?"

05:35 Diego: "We have three deployment modes: Hosted (fastest onboarding), Dedicated reserved capacity (predictable throughput on dedicated GPU pools), and Private (VPC/on-prem with private control plane). For VPC, we can set up secure peering and NAT, and provide audit logs. For on-prem we deliver a package that runs behind your firewall but it does require ops collaboration."

06:22 Samir: "Cool. Back to models — you mentioned benchmarking. Which open models do you usually start with for multilingual long context?"

06:35 Priya: "We often start with a 13B mixed-precision candidate that supports 32k context (some forks of LlamaX / Mistral variants), and a larger 70B context-capable model. For Chinese/Spanish coverage we evaluate model tokenizers and test with a bilingual eval set. Some customers also try quantized 13B 4-bit for cost savings."

07:05 Lena: "Does quantization impact tool-calling or streaming? We rely on low-latency streaming for the UI."

07:12 Diego: "Quantization can impact inference speed and sometimes affects quality; it doesn't break tool-calling. Streaming is about how the runtime emits tokens and is independent of quantization, though throughput and per-token latency are affected. Our runtime supports streaming responses and function-like tool calls."

08:00 Aisha: "Can you guarantee data residency in EU for Hosted?"

08:10 Maya: "Hosted can be region pinned in many cases — we have EU regions. For strict residency or regulated data, customers often choose Dedicated with dedicated capacity in the EU or Private with on-prem. We'll clarify the guarantees in the security doc."

09:02 Samir: "On cost - can you give a very rough ballpark for 13B quantized on Dedicated vs Hosted?"

09:10 Maya: "High level: Hosted is usage-based and easy to start; Dedicated is reserved monthly commits and becomes more cost-effective at scale. I'll include a pricing matrix. For a rough order, quantized 13B on Hosted might be X cents per 1k tokens, Dedicated per-token equivalent can be 30-50% lower depending on commit and batching. We'll provide ranges."

10:05 Tom: "What about batching — if we have many concurrent users, does Redwood do dynamic batching and prefix cache? We want predictable p95s."

10:15 Diego: "Yes, runtime supports continuous batching, prefix/KV caching for repeated contexts, and smart routing. You can tune batching thresholds to prioritize latency over throughput. For predictable p95, Dedicated with reservation and fixed pooling is often best."

11:00 Lena: "We frequently augment with retrieval; how does your RAG integration look — do you host the vector DB or integrate with Pinecone/Weaviate?"

11:12 Priya: "We integrate with common vector stores and you can host your own. For Private deployments we can co-locate retrieval. We also have built-in connectors and tool-calling hooks that can pass structured data into the model and handle tool responses."

12:01 Samir: "For POC we were thinking of three scenarios: 1) quick Hosted pilot for QA and UX; 2) Dedicated pilot with 2x A100-equivalent for production-like latency; 3) Private on-prem evaluation for EU-regulated docs. Can you support all three?"

12:20 Maya: "Yes to all three. Many customers start Hosted for speed, then move to Dedicated for scale and finally Private if they have strict compliance needs. We can design a migration path so you keep consistent APIs and rollouts."

13:30 Aisha: "On auditability — we need immutable audit logs and the ability to scrub PII. Is that exposed?"

13:40 Diego: "Audit logs are available in Console with per-request metadata. For PII scrubbing we can plugin redaction before persisting and we support configurable retention policies. For Private, since you're hosting control plane, you can set the retention as needed."

15:00 Lena: "We have multilingual benchmarks — we'll send 500 pairs (en/es/zh) and some long docs. For the long docs it's mostly legal contracts ~40-60k tokens, so 64k context would be ideal, otherwise we chunk. Any model recommendations for 64k?"

15:22 Priya: "There are a few 70B and some specialized long-context variants that support 64k. For many customers, a 13B 32k pipeline with smart retrieval works well; if you need native 64k to avoid stitching we should evaluate 70B variants. We'll test both with your data."

16:40 Tom: "Network egress for Hosted — does it pass content through public endpoints? We need to ensure the data doesn't route through US if EU-only."

16:52 Maya: "We can region-pin and ensure EU-only processing for Hosted; for strict no-egress, Private is recommended. We'll include a network diagram in the pack."

18:05 Samir: "Latency vs cost tradeoff question: if we use 7B quantized for chat (short queries) and route long docs to 70B, can Redwood do model routing automatically?"

18:18 Diego: "Yes, our routing policies can route by length, latency budget, or customer tier, and can fallback to smaller variants if capacity constrained. You can pin routes per endpoint."

20:00 Lena: "Tool calling: we need deterministic outputs for action triggering — sometimes hallucinations mean untrusted actions. How do you recommend enforcing safety for tool calls?"

20:15 Priya: "We recommend structured function schemas with model-side validation, pre-run guardrails (validate output vs schema), and a lightweight approval microservice for critical actions. Also run reranking/eval hooks to catch regressions."

22:00 Aisha: "For compliance we'll want data lineage — which user caused which tool call and what model generated it."

22:10 Diego: "All per-request metadata is captured: token counts, model variant, latency, the route and the user-id you pass. Those show up in Console traces and audit logs."

24:00 Samir: "What about SDKs — our stack is Node + Go. Any SDKs or templates?"

24:10 Maya: "We have REST plus official SDKs for Node and Python, and community Go samples. For Dedicated/Private we provide deployment templates and Terraform modules."

25:30 Tom: "SRE question — how do upgrades and model rollouts work? We need canary and quick rollback."

25:45 Diego: "We support canary rollouts, A/B tests, and automatic fallback policies. You can set traffic fractions per model version and rollback immediately if latency or quality regressions trigger alerts."

27:00 Lena: "Can we run a synthetic workload to measure p95 under expected concurrency?"

27:10 Diego: "Absolutely. We'll run bench harnesses against Dedicated pool or emulate on Hosted. We'll also test prefix caching and batching behavior with your workload profile."

29:00 Samir: "Timeline — we want a POC in the next 3 weeks if possible."

29:10 Maya: "That's feasible. Rough plan: week 1 - exchange artifacts and security review; week 2 - Redwood runs initial benchmarks and runs a Hosted pilot; week 3 - Dedicated pilot spin up if results look good. We'll sync on dates after this call."

31:00 Aisha: "One more on keys — if we use Dedicated can we bring our own KMS?"

31:08 Maya: "Yes, BYOK on Dedicated is supported; for Private obviously it's under your control. We'll document the exact flow for key rotations and access controls."

33:00 Lena: "Any gotchas you see with long-context handling that we should be aware of?"

33:12 Priya: "Memory and KV cache pressure is the big one. For 64k, the runtime needs more KV cache and we pay attention to sequence length distribution. Also prompt engineering to reduce redundant context helps. We'll show latency impact numbers in the benchmark."

35:00 Tom: "Does Redwood expose per-token cost breakdown? Our finance lead wants to estimate monthly spend."

35:12 Maya: "Yes, Console shows token-level cost and latency breakdowns per route/model and you can export reports. Redwood Optimize can also suggest batching/quantization to save costs."

36:40 Samir: "Are there reference customers who did a similar flow?"

36:50 Maya: "We can share anonymized case studies; I'll include a few references who ran mixed Hosted -> Dedicated -> Private migrations and had similar long-doc needs."

38:00 Lena: "Ok we'll prepare the eval set. One logistical: is there a limit on file sizes for uploads to the benchmarking harness?"

38:12 Diego: "We accept large documents; for very large single files we may chunk on ingestion. For benchmarking we'll accept your 40-60k token docs and run them natively against 64k-capable models where available."

40:00 Samir: "Security + procurement — we'll need a SOC 2 and a DPA draft. Procurement will also want pricing bands. Can you send that?"

40:10 Maya: "Yes, action item: I'll send security pack, SOC2 links, DPA template, and a high-level pricing sheet. Expect that by EOD tomorrow or latest Monday."

42:00 Tom: "If we do Dedicated POC what does the onboarding time look like?"

42:12 Maya: "Dedicated onboarding is typically 1-2 weeks once contract and capacity are provisioned; we can do faster for pilots with burst allocation. Private on-prem takes longer due to network setup."

44:00 Lena: "One small question — how often do you see quantization break subtle non-English syntactic behaviors?"

44:10 Priya: "It depends on the model and language. For some languages, lower-bit quantization can cause slight degradation; that's why we test bilingual evals. If you need parity, sometimes a larger model with light quantization is better than aggressive quant on a smaller model."

46:00 Samir: "Alright, let's summarize next steps."

46:10 Maya: "Recap: Redwood sends security pack, pricing matrix, and a suggested benchmark plan. Aurion sends prompt set, bilingual pairs, and long docs. Redwood runs initial benchmarks (13B quantized + 70B long variant), then we meet for SE deep-dive. Action items listed in the notes. Does that capture it?"

46:45 Samir: "Yes that looks right. One ask — can Diego include a short note on routing policies for traffic split?"

47:00 Diego: "Will do, I'll attach routing examples and an example policy that routes by token-length and latency budget."

48:00 Aisha: "Please also include the KMS and BYOK flow docs."

48:10 Maya: "Will do. Anything else?"

48:30 Tom: "Nope, thanks everyone."

49:00 Maya: "Thanks all, we'll follow up with the pack and propose times for the SE deep dive. Chat soon."

End of transcript.

Notes on transcript quality: medium - occasional speaker attribution errors, some technical terms slightly mis-transcribed (e.g., 'K V cache' or 'SAM L').
